tn.translation: In Longando there are essentially two tones, a high tone (´) and a low tone (`). (However, the low-tone symbols are generally omitted.) tn.quote: Il existe deux tons de base: bas et haut; et deux doubles: montant et descendant. La tonalité respecte l'allure générale du N tant pour les nominaux, les verbaux que pour les pronominaux. Quelques mots invariables étant propres au lonkutsu ont une tonalité particulière. Ajoutons plutSt qu'il a été constaté de légères différences tonales entre Ie pa~Ier d'Ok~la ett celui de Ohambe … Mais en réalité, dans beaucoup de cas il s'agit dans les deux parlers d'un ton pausal, c'est-à-dire qu'à la limite de l'énoncé Ie ton haut est réalisé plus ou moins bas.
tn.translation: There are two basic tones: low and high; and two double (compound) ones: rising and falling. Let us add rather that slight tonal differences have been noted between the Okala variety and that of Ohambe ... But in reality, in many cases what is involved in both varieties is a pausal tone, i.e. at the utterance boundary the high tone is realised more or less low.

5580.prule: Family-level rule (Chapakura; Oro Win measured in sec. 5.2): accent is predictable from syllable weight, the only prosodic factor: a light syllable is unstressed and low-toned, the heavy syllable (CVC, CVː, CVV), which always stands lexeme-final with at most one light syllable before it, is stressed and high-toned, so stress is invariably lexeme-final.

Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. … (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. … (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto.

tn.quote: Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. … A atualização fonética da acentuação lexical obedece às seguintes regras: (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. Em outras palavras, carrega um acento de intensidade (“stress”) fraco e um acento de altura (“pitch”) baixo; (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto. Em outras palavras, carrega um acento de intensidade (“stress”) forte e um acento de altura (“pitch”) alto.
tn.translation: In the Chapakura languages, the accentuation of lexemes is deducible from syllable weight - the only phonological prosodic factor in this language family. Accent is therefore not phonological, being predictable. … The phonetic realisation of lexical accentuation obeys the following rules: (a) a light syllable is unstressed and has a low tone; in other words it carries a weak intensity accent ('stress') and a low pitch accent; (b) a heavy syllable is stressed and has a high tone; in other words it carries a strong intensity accent ('stress') and a high pitch accent.

tn.translation: We have identified three phonemic level tones in Ngbugu: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]. Contour tones in Ngbugu are combinations of level tones, e.g. [vōtàá] 'three' (rising tone), [mīndúù] 'five' (falling tone). There are also long level tones, which we analyse as a sequence of level tones, e.g. [zòò] 'a long time'. … We have found tonal oppositions between words, e.g. [kú] 'bedbug', [kū] 'thigh', [kù] 'wound' (see table below). Since there are several tonal minimal pairs, all tones are written.

evidence_works.detail: Tone: the work states that 'musical syllable tone' is clearly distinguished besides the dynamic accent; tone minimal pairs exist but are said to be rarer than in some other West African languages (examples: nâse 'hand' vs násé 'foot'; ǹkídé 'mine' vs ǹkídà 'his'). Tone marks: high (acute), low (grave), mid (a third mark; glyph not certain from the scan), plus two compound tones low-high and high-low; a low-toned initial syllable is normally left unmarked. Tone sandhi: the mid-toned plural suffix -ba makes the preceding syllable high as a rule. Stress: the work says a dynamic accent (Starkton)
